Brain: The brain helps control thought, memory, speech, movement, and many organ functions. Nerves carry information between the brain and the rest of the body.
What should I know about headaches?
Headaches are common and have many possible causes. A tension headache can involve tight muscles in the neck, scalp, jaw, or shoulders.
Problems with attention or memory can have different causes. MedlinePlus has information about brain and nervous system conditions; a clinician can assess a new or persistent change.
Dizziness may feel like lightheadedness or unsteadiness. Vertigo is a spinning sensation even when nothing is moving; either can affect balance.
Heart: The heart and blood vessels make up the cardiovascular system, which circulates blood through the body.
A fast or noticeable heartbeat is called a palpitation. It can have different causes; a health professional can assess a new, persistent, or concerning change.
Chest pain has many possible causes, including heart, lung, digestive, and muscle problems. Sudden or severe chest pain needs urgent medical attention.
Fatigue means weariness or low energy. It can follow poor sleep or stress, but lasting fatigue can also signal a health problem.
Lungs: When you breathe, the lungs take oxygen from the air and pass it into your bloodstream. Lung conditions can make breathing difficult.
Coughing is a reflex that helps clear the throat and airways. Coughs may be short lived or last longer, and have different possible causes.
What can wheezing or chest tightness mean?
Wheezing and chest tightness can occur with breathing conditions. MedlinePlus lists several possible causes; a clinician can evaluate symptoms that are new or worsening.
Shortness of breath means breathing feels difficult or uncomfortable. It can follow exertion, but it can also signal a serious condition, especially if sudden or severe.
Kidney: The kidneys filter wastes and extra water from the blood. These leave the body as urine.
What can changes in urination mean?
Changes in how often you urinate, or in the urine itself, can have several causes. The kidneys make urine and the bladder stores it.
Kidney stones can cause severe pain when they block urine flow. Side or back pain has other possible causes too, so new or severe pain should be assessed.

Kidney disease can affect how the body handles extra fluid. Swelling has many causes and needs medical evaluation if new, persistent, or worsening.
Intestines: The digestive system absorbs nutrients and fluids from food and drink. The remaining waste leaves the body in a bowel movement.

Bloating can occur with digestive conditions. MedlinePlus notes it as one possible symptom of irritable bowel syndrome, alongside cramps and bowel habit changes; bloating alone does not establish a cause.
What are changes in bowel habits?
Constipation and diarrhea are changes in bowel movements. Persistent or significant changes can have many causes and deserve medical attention.
Abdominal pain can come from many organs, and its intensity does not always show how serious the cause is. Seek care for severe or persistent pain.
Stomach: The stomach stores swallowed food, mixes it with stomach acid, and passes the mixture to the small intestine.
Nausea is the feeling that you may vomit. It can occur with many conditions, including infections, migraines, motion sickness, and medicines.
Indigestion is discomfort or burning in the upper abdomen. It may come with bloating, belching, heartburn, or nausea.
What can feeling full quickly mean?
Feeling full sooner than expected is a digestive symptom with several possible causes. MedlinePlus covers stomach disorders broadly; a clinician can assess symptoms that persist or worsen.
full quickly early satiety appetite fullness
Liver: The liver helps digest food, stores energy, and removes harmful substances from the body.
Many organs can cause abdominal pain, so its location or intensity alone cannot identify the cause. Seek care for severe or persistent pain.
What can loss of appetite mean?
Liver diseases have different causes and symptoms. Loss of appetite is nonspecific; a clinician can assess a lasting change alongside other symptoms.
Fatigue is low energy or weariness. It has many possible causes, and weeks of unexplained fatigue warrant a conversation with a health professional.
Skin: Skin covers and protects the body, helps keep fluids in and germs out, and helps regulate temperature and sensation.
Dry skin is a common skin concern. Skin problems have many causes; persistent cracking, pain, or a changing rash may need assessment.
Itching is a sensation that makes you want to scratch. It may affect one area or the whole body and may occur with a rash or hives.
Redness can appear with many skin conditions, including irritation and infection. A rapidly spreading, painful, or fever associated change should be assessed promptly.
Spine: The spine is part of the nervous system's support and protection: the spinal cord carries signals between the brain and body.
Back pain can range from a dull ache to sudden sharp pain. It may be short lived or become chronic when it lasts more than three months.
Back pain and stiffness can affect movement. MedlinePlus describes many possible back problems; a clinician can assess symptoms that persist or limit daily activities.
Back problems may make bending, walking, or other movements difficult. New weakness, numbness, or loss of bladder or bowel control requires urgent assessment.
Bladder: The bladder is a hollow organ in the lower abdomen that stores urine before you urinate.
Frequent urination can occur with several bladder or urinary conditions. MedlinePlus describes overactive bladder as one possible explanation, but frequency alone cannot identify the cause.
Bladder discomfort has several possible causes, including inflammation or infection. A clinician can assess pain, fever, or other new urinary symptoms.
Urgency is a sudden strong need to urinate. It can occur with overactive bladder and other conditions; new symptoms deserve evaluation.
Knee: The knee joint contains bone, cartilage, ligaments, and fluid; muscles and tendons help it move.
Knee problems can cause pain and difficulty walking. Stiffness has several possible causes, so persistent or worsening symptoms should be assessed.
Swelling may occur when knee structures are injured or inflamed. A markedly swollen knee or one you cannot bear weight on needs prompt evaluation.
Bone, cartilage, ligaments, muscles, and tendons all help the knee move. Pain with movement can involve different structures and cannot be identified from a symptom alone.
Head: What structures are in the head?
The brain is the body's control center, and nerves carry sensory information to it. Head symptoms can also involve the eyes, ears, nose, or other structures.

Eye: How do I care for my eyes?
Eye care includes daily habits and regular examinations. Some eye diseases have no early warning signs, so checkups matter even when vision seems fine.
Dry or irritated eyes can have several causes. MedlinePlus covers eye care and conditions; ongoing discomfort can be assessed by an eye care professional.
Eye strain can follow prolonged close work or screen use. Persistent pain or any change in vision should be assessed rather than assumed to be strain.
Eye irritation has different possible causes, including dryness or infection. Pain, injury, or a sudden vision change needs prompt eye care.
Ear: The ear has outer, middle, and inner parts that support hearing; inner ear structures also help with balance.
Ear pain or discomfort can occur with different ear problems, including infections. Persistent pain, drainage, or hearing change should be assessed.
What is ringing in the ears?
Ringing or other sound heard without an outside source is called tinnitus. It can have several causes, so a clinician can assess persistent or new symptoms.
What can a blocked ear sensation mean?
A blocked sensation may come with ear conditions or hearing changes. Sudden hearing loss needs prompt medical attention.
Throat: The throat carries food toward the esophagus and air toward the windpipe and voice box.
Sore throat can have many causes, including colds, flu, allergies, and infections. The cause determines the appropriate care.
Hoarseness is a voice change that can have several causes. MedlinePlus provides information on throat and voice disorders; a persistent change should be assessed.
Swallowing problems can involve pain or difficulty with food, liquids, or saliva. If you cannot swallow or have breathing trouble, seek urgent care.
Tooth: How can I care for my teeth?
MedlinePlus recommends brushing with fluoride toothpaste twice daily and cleaning between teeth every day as part of dental care.
tooth teeth dental health function care
Tooth sensitivity can occur with several dental problems. Tooth decay damages enamel and can eventually cause pain; a dentist can find the cause.
Tooth decay can lead to cavities, pain, and infection. Tooth pain has other possible causes too and should be evaluated by a dentist.
Gum disease affects tissues around the teeth. Bleeding, swelling, or persistent irritation should be discussed with a dental professional.
Shoulder: The shoulder is a highly movable joint. Muscles, tendons, and ligaments help hold it in place and allow movement.
Shoulder problems can affect movement and cause stiffness or pain. Several structures can be involved, so persistent symptoms need assessment.
The shoulder's muscles and tendons help move the arm. Pain with lifting may involve different structures and cannot be diagnosed from that symptom alone.
A shoulder injury or disorder may restrict arm movement. New severe pain, deformity, or inability to move the arm needs prompt assessment.
